propositions: Guidance must require rebar tracker operations (claim, transition, link, review-plan, verify-completion, etc.) to route through the MCP server when configured, with an explicit carve-out for local-code operations (testing, investigation, debugging, validation).

AGENTS.md must establish an umbrella rule governing downstream guidance surfaces (docs/, templates/, .agents/rules/, packaged rebar explain guides, example skills) such that rebar tracker-op verbs named in those surfaces route through MCP without requiring individual rewrites of each surface.

Certified operations comprise only plan-review and completion-verifier (per ADR 0049), both MCP-routed and enforceable via trusted-env registration; code review is the Gerrit LLM-Review vote, not an op-cert, and no guidance must assert a code-review op-cert exists.
Certified-op enforcement must be described as enableable but deferred, not live, with a citation to the mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md runbook.

docs/mcp-auth.md §7 must document the AWS deployment recipe using ADR-decided config keys (http_tls_at_edge, auth_static_tokens_file, auth_strategies) and must link to docs/mcp-client-setup.md for client connection config shapes (copilot, codex, claude).

A follow-up ticket must be created to perform a per-file reconciliation sweep of non-doc surfaces (templates/, .agents/rules/, packaged guides, example skills) to align their rebar tracker-op mentions with the umbrella rule.
